notice: 40 recipes: 12 original Weektable recipes and 28 independently written adaptations from Striped Spatula and Just One Cookbook. Ratings describe the original source recipes as of 2026-10-26. Source rights and linked policies remain applicable. No Mealime recipes are included.

recipes.title: Lemon chicken & herby couscous
recipes.description: A bright skillet dinner with tender chicken, fluffy couscous and crisp cucumber.
steps: Set out the ingredients and boil water for the couscous. Follow the packet for the water amount; different couscous types need different ratios.
Cut the chicken into even strips. Keep the chicken board and knife separate from the vegetables.
Finely chop the garlic. Zest the lemon, then cut it in half. Toss the chicken with half the oil, the garlic, lemon zest, salt and pepper.
Put the couscous in a heatproof bowl, add the packet-directed amount of boiling water and cover.
Heat a wide frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken in a single layer; cook in batches if needed.
Turn the chicken as it browns and cook until its centre reaches 74°C. Remove it to a clean plate.
Dice the cucumber and tomatoes. Chop the parsley. Fluff the couscous and mix in the vegetables, parsley, remaining oil and lemon juice.
Divide the couscous between plates and add the chicken. For larger batches, allow extra pan time and cook the chicken in batches.

recipes.title: Roasted salmon, broccoli & rice
recipes.description: One oven tray, a pot of rice and a simple lemon-mustard dressing.
steps: Heat the oven to 210°C and line a baking tray.
Cook the rice with water according to its packet directions.
Cut the broccoli into small florets. Slice the stalk thinly after removing its tough outer layer.
Toss the broccoli with half the oil and half the salt and spread it over the tray. Roast for 10 minutes.
Mix the remaining oil with the mustard, honey, juice from half the lemon and the pepper.
Move the broccoli aside. Put the salmon on the tray, season with the remaining salt and brush with the dressing.
Return the tray to the oven until the salmon reaches 63°C in its thickest part and the broccoli is tender, roughly 10–15 minutes depending on thickness.
Fluff the rice and serve with the salmon, broccoli and the remaining lemon cut into wedges. Use an additional tray for a larger batch.

recipes.title: Smoky black bean tacos
recipes.description: Warm tortillas filled with cumin beans, crunchy cabbage and lime yogurt.
steps: Drain and rinse the beans. Finely chop the onion and garlic.
Thinly slice the cabbage. Cut the avocado into slices and cut the lime in half.
Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft, then add the garlic, cumin and paprika.
Stir for 30 seconds, then add the beans, half the salt and a small splash of water.
Simmer gently for 5 minutes. Mash some beans with a spoon so the filling holds together.
Mix the yogurt with lime juice and the remaining salt. Keep some lime juice aside for the cabbage.
Warm the tortillas in a dry frying pan or according to their packet directions. Toss the cabbage with the reserved lime juice.
Fill the tortillas with beans, cabbage, avocado and lime yogurt. Keep the components separate until serving.

recipes.title: Creamy tomato & spinach pasta
recipes.description: A comforting tomato sauce finished with cream cheese and a handful of spinach.
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Cook the pasta according to its packet directions.
Peel and finely chop the garlic. Rinse the spinach and grate the Parmesan.
Warm the oil in a wide saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic and stir until fragrant, without letting it brown.
Add the tomatoes, oregano, salt and pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 8 minutes.
Stir in the cream cheese until it melts into the sauce.
Before draining the pasta, save a mug of its cooking water.
Add the spinach to the sauce and stir until wilted. Fold in the drained pasta, loosening with a little reserved pasta water as needed.
Divide into bowls and finish with the Parmesan. Larger batches may need a larger pan for easy mixing.

recipes.title: Sesame tofu rice bowls
recipes.description: Crisp-edged tofu with broccoli, carrots and a glossy ginger-soy sauce.
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet directions.
Drain the tofu, pat it dry and cut into bite-size cubes. Toss with the cornstarch.
Cut the broccoli into small florets and the carrots into thin slices. Finely chop the garlic and ginger.
Mix the soy sauce, rice vinegar, maple syrup and sesame oil in a bowl.
Heat the neutral oil in a wide frying pan. Add the tofu in a single layer and turn until golden on several sides. Transfer to a plate.
Add the broccoli and carrots to the pan with a splash of water. Cover briefly to steam, then uncover and cook until just tender.
Add the garlic and ginger. Stir for 30 seconds, return the tofu and pour in the sauce. Toss until everything is coated and hot.
Serve over the rice with sesame seeds. Use batches when scaling up so the tofu has room to brown.

recipes.title: Turkey & sweet potato skillet
recipes.description: A hearty one-pan dinner with peppers, cumin and a little melted cheddar.
steps: Peel the sweet potato and cut it into small, even cubes. Dice the onion and bell pepper and finely chop the garlic.
Heat half the oil in a large lidded frying pan over medium heat. Add the sweet potato and a splash of water.
Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until the potato is nearly tender. Add a little more water if the pan dries out.
Move the potato to a plate. Add the remaining oil, onion and pepper to the pan and cook until softened.
Add the turkey and break it up with a spoon. Cook until browned and the turkey reaches 74°C.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, paprika, salt and pepper, then return the sweet potato to the pan.
Cook until the potato is tender and everything is piping hot. Grate the cheese over the top.
Cover briefly to melt the cheese, then serve. With more servings, use a larger pan or two pans so the turkey cooks evenly.

recipes.title: Chickpea & spinach coconut curry
recipes.description: A gentle coconut curry with chickpeas, tomatoes and soft spinach.
steps: Cook the rice according to its packet directions.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Chop the onion and finely chop the garlic and ginger.
Warm the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger and curry powder and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, coconut milk, chickpeas and salt. Stir well and bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer uncovered for about 12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens slightly.
Rinse the spinach, stir it into the curry and cook until wilted. Add a small splash of water if the sauce becomes too thick.
Serve the curry alongside the rice. Refrigerate leftovers promptly in shallow containers.

recipes.title: Ginger beef & mushroom noodles
recipes.description: Quick noodles with tender beef strips, mushrooms and a savoury soy glaze.
steps: Cook the noodles according to their packet directions, then drain.
Slice the mushrooms and cut the carrots into thin matchsticks. Finely chop the garlic and ginger.
Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, honey and cornstarch with a little water to make a pourable sauce.
Heat half the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Add the beef in batches and cook to your required safe doneness, then transfer to a clean plate.
Add the remaining oil to the pan. Cook the mushrooms and carrots until the mushrooms have browned and the carrots are tender-crisp.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds.
Return the beef and any collected juices. Stir the sauce again, pour it into the pan and heat until bubbling and slightly thickened.
Add the noodles and toss until hot throughout. A larger batch is easier to combine in a large pot after cooking the beef in batches.

recipes.title: Roasted vegetable, quinoa & feta bowls
recipes.description: Colourful roasted vegetables with quinoa, chickpeas and lemony feta.
steps: Heat the oven to 210°C. Line a large baking tray.
Rinse the quinoa and cook it according to the packet directions.
Cut the zucchini and pepper into bite-size pieces. Peel the onion and cut it into wedges.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Dry them lightly with a clean towel.
Spread the vegetables and chickpeas over the tray. Toss with the oil, oregano, salt and pepper.
Roast for 20–25 minutes, turning once, until the vegetables are tender and browned at the edges.
Fluff the quinoa. Crumble the feta and squeeze the lemon.
Build bowls with quinoa, vegetables and chickpeas. Finish with feta and lemon juice. Use two trays for more servings rather than crowding one.

recipes.title: Egg & vegetable fried rice
recipes.description: A flexible skillet supper with eggs, peas, carrots and spring onions.

ingredients.name: cooked long-grain rice
ingredients.note: Use promptly chilled cooked rice, or freshly cooked rice spread briefly to steam-dry.

steps: Use cooked rice that has been safely chilled, or freshly cooked rice spread on a tray just long enough to release excess steam. Do not leave cooked rice sitting at room temperature.
Dice the carrots small. Slice the spring onions and chop the garlic.
Beat the eggs in a bowl. Heat a little of the neutral oil in a wide frying pan.
Scramble the eggs until set and transfer them to a plate.
Add the remaining neutral oil, carrots and peas. Stir-fry until the carrots are tender, adding a splash of water if needed.
Add the garlic and most of the spring onions. Stir briefly, then add the rice and break up clumps.
Add the soy sauce, sesame oil and scrambled eggs. Stir-fry until the rice is piping hot throughout; reheat chilled leftovers to 74°C.
Serve immediately with the remaining spring onions. Cook larger quantities in batches to heat the rice evenly.

recipes.title: Lemony white bean & vegetable soup
recipes.description: A simple pot of white beans, carrots and spinach with toast on the side.
steps: Peel and dice the onion and carrots. Finely chop the garlic.
Drain and rinse the beans. Rinse the spinach.
Warm the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrots for several minutes until the onion softens.
Add the garlic and thyme and stir for 30 seconds.
Pour in the vegetable stock and add the beans. Bring to a simmer.
Cook gently until the carrots are tender, about 15 minutes. Mash a spoonful of beans against the side of the pan for a slightly thicker soup.
Stir in the spinach and pepper, then add lemon juice to taste from the measured lemon. Heat until the spinach wilts.
Toast the bread and serve it alongside the soup. Taste before adding any extra salt because stocks vary in saltiness.

recipes.title: Chicken fajita wraps
recipes.description: Sizzling chicken and peppers with cool yogurt and a squeeze of lime.
steps: Slice the peppers and onion into strips. Set them aside.
Using a separate board, cut the chicken into thin, even strips.
Toss the chicken with half the oil, the cumin, paprika, salt and pepper.
Heat a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken in batches until lightly browned and its centre reaches 74°C. Transfer to a clean plate.
Add the remaining oil to the pan. Cook the peppers and onion until softened and lightly browned.
Return the chicken to the pan and squeeze over half the lime. Toss until everything is hot.
Warm the tortillas according to their packet directions. Mix the yogurt with juice from the remaining lime.
Fill the warm tortillas with chicken and peppers and spoon on the lime yogurt. Keep any extra filling separate until serving.

recipes.title: Butter shoyu chicken
recipes.description: Chicken with a butter, sake and soy glaze. Main dish only; sides are separate.

ingredients.name: Diamond Crystal kosher salt
ingredients.note: For table salt, use half this volume.

ingredients.name: sake
ingredients.note: Two-thirds for steaming; one-third for sauce.

steps: Halve the thighs, trim excess fat and prick the skin. Apply the salt and pepper.
Dissolve sugar in soy sauce, mirin and one-third of the sake.
Heat oil over medium heat. Brown chicken skin-side down for 4–5 minutes, then turn and cook another 3 minutes. Work in batches if necessary.
Pour in the remaining sake, cover and cook until the liquid evaporates and chicken reaches 74°C / 165°F.
Remove excess fat. Add the sauce and butter; simmer while spooning the glaze over the chicken. Serve.

source.adaptations: Independently condensed instructions. Sake entries combined; poultry temperature check added. Unspecified sides omitted.

recipes.title: Oyakodon — chicken & egg rice bowls
recipes.description: Chicken, onion and egg over rice.

ingredients.name: cooked Japanese short-grain rice
ingredients.note: Ready-to-heat rice; or prepare separately. This is cooked weight.

steps: Warm the prepared rice. Slice onion, chop mitsuba and cut chicken into small, even pieces. Coat chicken with sake for 5 minutes.
Combine dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar. Loosely break up the eggs.
Place onions and sauce in a pan; bring to a simmer. Add chicken and simmer uncovered about 5 minutes, turning once, until it reaches 74°C / 165°F.
Pour in two-thirds of the egg. When partly set, add the rest and mitsuba. Cook until egg is set.
Spoon over rice. For larger quantities, use separate pans or cook in batches of two servings.

source.name: Just One Cookbook
source.license: Factual recipe adaptation for personal, noncommercial use; source rights retained
source.attribution: Namiko Hirasawa Chen / Just One Cookbook
source.adaptations: Independently condensed instructions. Uses 4 eggs from the source range of 3–4. Cooked rice uses the source gram measure; optional spices omitted. Eggs cooked through.

recipes.title: Chicken teriyaki
recipes.description: Pan-cooked chicken with a soy and mirin glaze. Main dish only; sides are separate.

ingredients.name: Diamond Crystal kosher salt
ingredients.note: For table salt, use half this volume.

steps: Warm soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar together just enough to dissolve the sugar.
Make shallow cuts across thick parts of the chicken and flatten to an even thickness. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil over medium-high heat. Place thighs smooth-side down, press briefly and brown about 5 minutes.
Turn, reduce to low, cover and cook about 3 minutes. Remove excess grease.
Add sauce over medium heat, spooning it over the chicken until glazed and the meat reaches 74°C / 165°F. Reduce sauce further if needed, then slice and serve.

source.name: Just One Cookbook
source.license: Factual recipe adaptation for personal, noncommercial use; source rights retained
source.attribution: Namiko Hirasawa Chen / Just One Cookbook
source.adaptations: Independently condensed instructions. Uses 1 lb from source range ¾–1 lb; skinless method. Optional torch finish and unquantified sides omitted.

recipes.title: Gyudon — Japanese beef rice bowls
recipes.description: Thin beef and onions in a sweet soy broth over rice.

ingredients.name: cooked Japanese short-grain rice
ingredients.note: Ready-to-heat rice; or prepare separately. This is cooked weight.

steps: Warm the prepared rice. Slice onion and scallion; separate the thin beef slices.
In a cold frying pan, stir together dashi, sake, mirin, soy sauce and sugar.
Spread onion through the liquid, then arrange beef on top. Cover and heat over medium.
Once simmering, lower heat and cook 3–4 minutes, until onion softens and beef is cooked. Skim excess foam or fat.
Scatter scallion over the pan and cook covered for another minute. Portion rice into bowls and add beef, onion and some broth.

source.name: Just One Cookbook
source.license: Factual recipe adaptation for personal, noncommercial use; source rights retained
source.attribution: Namiko Hirasawa Chen / Just One Cookbook
source.adaptations: Independently condensed instructions. Uses the source cooked-rice weight. Optional pickled-ginger garnish omitted; no dry-rice conversion assumed.

recipes.title: Hambagu — Japanese hamburger steaks
recipes.description: Beef and pork patties with pan sauce; sides separate.

ingredients.name: neutral oil
ingredients.note: Half for onion; half for patties.

ingredients.name: Diamond Crystal kosher salt
ingredients.note: For table salt, use half this volume.

ingredients.name: red wine
ingredients.note: Half for steaming; half for sauce.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: Add a little more only if needed.

steps: Soften onion in half the oil; cool. Knead with both meats, salt, pepper, nutmeg, panko, milk and egg until sticky.
Shape one oval patty per serving; expel air. Chill 30 minutes.
Heat remaining oil over medium. Indent centres; brown patties 3 minutes per side in batches.
Add half the wine; cover and cook on low 5–7 minutes to 71°C / 160°F. Remove patties.
Simmer butter, ketchup, tonkatsu sauce, remaining wine and water until thickened. Spoon over patties.

source.name: Just One Cookbook
source.license: Factual recipe adaptation for personal, noncommercial use; source rights retained
source.attribution: Namiko Hirasawa Chen / Just One Cookbook
source.adaptations: Condensed method; source 2:1 beef:pork option. Minimum water; sides omitted. Total includes 30-minute chilling. Temperature check added.

recipes.title: Soboro don — chicken & egg bowls
recipes.description: Fine chicken crumbles, scrambled egg and peas over rice.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: Half for chicken; half for eggs.

ingredients.name: Diamond Crystal kosher salt
ingredients.note: For table salt, use half this volume.

ingredients.name: cooked Japanese short-grain rice
ingredients.note: Ready-to-heat rice; or prepare separately. This is cooked weight.

steps: Warm the prepared rice and peas. Combine chicken, ginger, sake, mirin, soy sauce and half the sugar in a cold saucepan.
Set over medium-low heat. Stir and break up chicken for 3–4 minutes; continue 2–3 minutes until most liquid evaporates and meat reaches 74°C / 165°F.
In another cold saucepan, whisk eggs with remaining sugar and salt.
Cook eggs over medium-low heat, stirring and scraping into small curds until set.
Divide rice among bowls, arrange chicken and egg on top, and finish with peas.

source.name: Just One Cookbook
source.license: Factual recipe adaptation for personal, noncommercial use; source rights retained
source.attribution: Namiko Hirasawa Chen / Just One Cookbook
source.adaptations: Independently condensed instructions. Uses the lower chicken-sugar amount, 1 tbsp; combined sugar total includes the eggs. Ginger uses the source grated measure; optional ginger pickle omitted.

recipes.title: Pan-fried curry chicken
recipes.description: Lightly coated chicken pieces with a Japanese curry glaze. Main dish only; sides separate.

ingredients.name: Diamond Crystal kosher salt
ingredients.note: For table salt, use half this volume.

steps: Stir soy sauce, mirin, curry powder and sugar together.
Remove tough tendons and cut chicken into thin, even pieces. Season, coat with mayonnaise, then toss with flour in two additions.
Work in two-serving batches. Heat oil over medium; fry chicken 3 minutes, turn and cook 2 minutes, until 74°C / 165°F.
Wipe pan clean. Simmer some sauce; return chicken and toss to coat.
Add more sauce only as needed; taste before adding the rest. Avoid over-reducing, and loosen with water if necessary.

source.name: Just One Cookbook
source.license: Factual recipe adaptation for personal, noncommercial use; source rights retained
source.attribution: Namiko Hirasawa Chen / Just One Cookbook
source.adaptations: Independently condensed instructions. Optional dipping mayonnaise, garnish and unquantified sides omitted. Poultry-temperature check added. Source cautions that scaled sauce may be salty; quantities remain linear estimates.

recipes.title: Japanese chicken curry
recipes.description: Chicken, potato and carrot curry with prepared rice.

ingredients.name: cooked Japanese short-grain rice
ingredients.note: Ready-to-heat rice; or prepare separately. This is cooked weight.

steps: Chop onions, carrots, potatoes and chicken. Soak potatoes 15 minutes, then drain. Grate apple and ginger; mince garlic. Season chicken with pepper.
Soften onion in oil over medium heat for 5 minutes. Add garlic, ginger and chicken; stir until chicken changes colour outside.
Add broth, apple, honey, soy sauce, ketchup, carrots and potatoes. Simmer covered for 15 minutes, then until vegetables are tender and chicken reaches 74°C / 165°F.
Off heat, dissolve curry blocks in a little hot broth and stir back in.
Simmer uncovered 5–10 minutes, stirring; add water if too thick. Serve with warmed rice.

source.name: Just One Cookbook
source.license: Factual recipe adaptation for personal, noncommercial use; source rights retained
source.attribution: Namiko Hirasawa Chen / Just One Cookbook
source.adaptations: Independently condensed instructions. Chooses 200 g roux from source range 200–230 g. App specifies cooked rice at 200 g per person; source gives portions without weight. Pickles omitted.

recipes.title: Beef and Broccoli
recipes.description: Steak and broccoli stir-fry; rice is separate.
steps: Coat beef with two-fifths of cornstarch, two-thirds of light soy, water and rice wine. Marinate 15–20 minutes.
Combine remaining cornstarch and light soy with broth, oyster sauce, dark soy, sesame oil, sugar and scallion whites.
Pat beef dry; brown over high heat in batches, 2 minutes each, using two-fifths of oil. Remove.
Stir-fry broccoli with another two-fifths of oil for 2–4 minutes. Clear center; cook remaining oil, ginger and garlic there 30 seconds.
Return beef and juices. Rewhisk sauce; add, reduce heat to medium and stir 1–2 minutes until thickened. Add scallion greens.

source.name: Striped Spatula
source.license: Adapted under source sharing guidelines; original source rights retained
source.attribution: Amanda Biddle / Striped Spatula
source.adaptations: Method condensed. Lower sauce-soy quantity selected. Rice and optional pepper omitted.

recipes.title: Ground Beef Stroganoff
recipes.description: One-pan beef, mushrooms and noodles; four generous portions.
steps: Season beef; brown in oil over medium-high heat, breaking into crumbles. Remove, leaving drippings.
Add butter if needed; cook onion, mushrooms and measured seasoning until their liquid evaporates. Stir garlic 30 seconds.
Add cognac; scrape pan and evaporate. Return beef; stir flour 1–2 minutes.
Add seven-eighths of broth, mustard, Worcestershire, paprika, two-thirds of thyme and noodles. Submerge noodles; boil, cover and simmer 7–10 minutes until tender; stir occasionally.
Add reserved broth if drying. Off heat, fold in sour cream, remaining thyme and two-thirds of parsley. Season; garnish with remaining parsley.

source.name: Striped Spatula
source.license: Adapted under source sharing guidelines; original source rights retained
source.attribution: Amanda Biddle / Striped Spatula
source.adaptations: Source yield 4–6; app uses 4 generous portions. Lower butter, oil, paprika and cream chosen; full broth allowance. Optional lemon omitted.

recipes.title: Pork Chops Marsala
recipes.description: Pork with a mushroom cream sauce; sides are separate.
steps: Keep one-third of the flour for the sauce. Season the pork and dust it with the rest.
Heat butter and oil over medium-high heat. Brown chops for 3–4 minutes per side, reaching 63°C/145°F. Set aside.
Cook mushrooms and shallot with measured salt and pepper for 5 minutes. Stir in reserved flour for 1 minute.
Add Marsala; scrape the pan for 1–2 minutes. Pour in stock and simmer 5–8 minutes.
Mix in cream and herbs. Return pork and juices; simmer 2 minutes. Adjust seasoning and serve.

source.name: Striped Spatula
source.license: Adapted under source sharing guidelines; original source rights retained
source.attribution: Amanda Biddle / Striped Spatula
source.adaptations: Instructions independently condensed. Mushrooms set to the upper end of the source range. Optional garnish and sides omitted.

recipes.title: Maine Lobster Rolls
recipes.description: Chilled lobster salad in buttered buns.
steps: Check the cooked lobster carefully for stray shell. Cut the meat into large chunks.
Fold in three-quarters of the mayonnaise. Add the remainder only if needed, then season to taste.
Cover and refrigerate the filling for at least 30 minutes.
Heat a griddle to medium. Butter the outside faces of the buns and toast each side for a few minutes.
Divide the chilled lobster among the warm buns and serve.

source.name: Striped Spatula
source.license: Adapted under source sharing guidelines; original source rights retained
source.attribution: Amanda Biddle / Striped Spatula
source.adaptations: Instructions independently condensed. Mayonnaise uses the upper range. Optional celery, lettuce and lemon omitted. Source timing includes preparing lobster; the app starts with cooked meat.

recipes.title: Linguine with Clams
recipes.description: Clams, white wine and parsley with linguine.
steps: Discard cracked clams and open ones that will not close when tapped. Scrub; refrigerate in cold saltwater 30 minutes (⅓ US cup non-iodized salt per US gallon). Lift out; repeat with fresh brine if gritty. Rinse.
Boil pasta until just short of tender. Save some cooking water before draining.
Warm oil; cook garlic and pepper flakes 1–2 minutes. Add wine, lemon juice and clams; cover.
Steam 5–8 minutes, removing opened clams promptly. Discard any still closed after 13 minutes.
Melt butter into the liquid. Toss in pasta for 2 minutes, loosening with reserved water. Add parsley, clams and salt; serve.

source.name: Striped Spatula
source.license: Adapted under source sharing guidelines; original source rights retained
source.attribution: Amanda Biddle / Striped Spatula
source.adaptations: Instructions independently condensed. Clams and garlic use upper ranges; pepper uses lower range. Extra oil, lemon wedges and bread omitted.

recipes.title: Shrimp Lo Mein
recipes.description: Shrimp noodles with crisp vegetables. Four generous portions.
steps: Boil noodles 3–5 minutes until firm-tender; drain and rinse cool. Mix both soy sauces, wine, oyster sauce, sugar, sesame oil and pepper.
Slice scallion whites; cut greens into short lengths. Heat a wok until very hot.
Use one-third of the vegetable oil to stir-fry carrots, peas, chestnuts and bamboo for 2 minutes; remove.
Add another third of oil. Cook shrimp 2–3 minutes until opaque; remove.
With remaining oil, fry scallion whites, garlic and ginger 1 minute. Add everything else; toss with sauce 1–2 minutes.

source.name: Striped Spatula
source.license: Adapted under source sharing guidelines; original source rights retained
source.attribution: Amanda Biddle / Striped Spatula
source.adaptations: Instructions independently condensed. Source serves 4–6; app selects 4 larger portions. Fresh noodles selected. Optional table sauces omitted.

recipes.title: Teriyaki Salmon
recipes.description: Pan-seared salmon with a soy glaze; sides are separate.

ingredients.name: sake
ingredients.note: Half for sauce, half for steaming

steps: Combine half the sake with mirin, soy sauce and sugar; stir until dissolved.
Pat salmon dry, season with salt and pepper, then coat lightly with flour.
Warm oil and butter over medium heat. Sear salmon skin-side down 3 minutes, then turn.
Add remaining sake, cover and lower heat. Steam about 3–5 minutes; check the thickest part reaches 63°C/145°F. Remove fish.
Bring the sauce to a boil in the pan. Return salmon briefly, spooning the glaze over it as it thickens.

source.name: Just One Cookbook
source.license: Factual recipe adaptation for personal, noncommercial use; source rights retained
source.attribution: Namiko Hirasawa Chen / Just One Cookbook
source.adaptations: Instructions independently condensed. Uses the source-mentioned 63°C fish safety endpoint, rather than its preferred lower endpoint. Sides omitted.

recipes.title: Miso Salmon
recipes.description: Miso-marinated salmon; allow at least one hour to marinate.
steps: Remove any pin bones or scales. Stir miso, sake, mirin, soy sauce and sesame oil into a marinade.
Coat the salmon, cover and refrigerate 1–2 hours.
Preheat the broiler on high for 5 minutes, with the rack about 23 cm below it. Oil a foil-lined metal tray.
Scrape excess marinade off the fish and discard it. Set salmon skin-side down. Broil around 10–13 minutes, checking until the centre reaches 63°C/145°F.
Scatter sesame seeds and scallion over the fish. Rice and other sides are separate.

source.name: Just One Cookbook
source.license: Factual recipe adaptation for personal, noncommercial use; source rights retained
source.attribution: Namiko Hirasawa Chen / Just One Cookbook
source.adaptations: Instructions independently condensed. 80 minutes includes minimum marinating time. Uses 63°C fish endpoint; garnish included. Rice omitted.

recipes.title: Ginger Pork (Shogayaki)
recipes.description: Thin pork slices in ginger sauce; sides are separate.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger juice
ingredients.note: Squeeze grated ginger; roughly a 5 cm piece

steps: Combine soy sauce, mirin, sugar, two-thirds of the sake and half the ginger juice. Grate a little onion into this sauce; slice the rest.
Coat pork with remaining sake and ginger juice. Wait 5 minutes, then dust lightly with flour.
Heat oil over medium-high heat. Brown pork in uncrowded batches, turning once; set aside.
Cook sliced onion over medium heat for 6–8 minutes. Return pork and pour in the stirred sauce.
Simmer about 2 minutes, coating the pork, until it reaches 63°C/145°F and the sauce thickens. Rest 3 minutes.

source.name: Just One Cookbook
source.license: Factual recipe adaptation for personal, noncommercial use; source rights retained
source.attribution: Namiko Hirasawa Chen / Just One Cookbook
source.adaptations: Instructions independently condensed. Oil uses upper range; optional ginger pulp and pepper omitted. Rice and cabbage omitted.

recipes.title: Tonteki Pork Steaks
recipes.description: Pork with ponzu sauce, cabbage and tomato.
steps: Grate half the onion wedge, keeping the rest for another use. Shred cabbage and cut tomato into wedges.
Mix ponzu, sake and soy sauce.
Pat chops dry. Snip the connective tissue at their edges, season and lightly flour them.
Heat oil over medium-high heat. Brown chops roughly 4 minutes per side, working in batches.
Add sauce and grated onion; spoon over pork until hot. Ensure pork reaches 63°C/145°F and rests 3 minutes. Serve with cabbage and tomato.

source.name: Just One Cookbook
source.license: Factual recipe adaptation for personal, noncommercial use; source rights retained
source.attribution: Namiko Hirasawa Chen / Just One Cookbook
source.adaptations: Instructions independently condensed. Optional cabbage and tomato included; parsley omitted. Source onion wedge includes a grating handhold.

recipes.title: Cream of Mushroom Soup
recipes.description: Creamy mushroom soup; bread is separate.
steps: Soften onion in butter over medium heat for 5–8 minutes.
Add mushrooms, salt and pepper. Cook 8–10 minutes, letting moisture evaporate and edges brown.
Stir in flour for 1 minute, then sherry for 1 minute, loosening browned bits.
Add broth and thyme. Bring to a boil, then simmer 20 minutes.
Cool slightly; blend a portion with a vented blender and return it to the pot. Stir in cream and warm gently without boiling; adjust seasoning.

source.name: Striped Spatula
source.license: Adapted under source sharing guidelines; original source rights retained
source.attribution: Amanda Biddle / Striped Spatula

recipes.title: Sun-Dried Tomato Pasta Salad
recipes.description: Pasta, artichokes, herbs and pine nuts.
steps: Blend half the tomatoes with lemon, garlic, mustard, salt and pepper. Blend in four-fifths of the oil; pulse in oregano.
Cook pasta al dente; drain, rinse and cool.
Heat remaining oil over medium-high heat. Brown artichokes for 5–8 minutes. Loosen pan juices with a splash of water for 1 minute.
Off heat, add shallots, capers and remaining tomatoes, sliced. Toss with pasta, dressing, nuts, herbs and cheese.

recipes.title: Chickpea and Feta Salad
recipes.description: Lemon-dressed chickpeas for a light meal; bread is separate.
steps: Dry the chickpeas and remove loose skins.
Whisk oil, lemon, garlic, salt and pepper until combined.
Coat chickpeas and parsley with the dressing. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Fold in feta before serving. Taste and adjust seasoning.

recipes.title: Soba Noodle Salad
recipes.description: Sesame-dressed noodles with herbs.
steps: Warm both oils with pepper flakes over medium heat for 3 minutes, avoiding scorching. Remove from heat; cool 1–2 minutes.
Whisk honey into the warm oil, then add soy sauce carefully.
Cook noodles in unsalted water until al dente, about 30 seconds short of package timing. Rinse cold and drain thoroughly.
Slice onions and chop cilantro. Toss noodles with dressing, herbs and sesame seeds; serve cool or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Vegetarian Ramen
recipes.description: Soy-milk broth, noodles and bok choy.
steps: Soak kombu and shiitake in water 30 minutes. Heat to just below boiling; remove solids and replenish evaporated water.
Grind sesame. Sauté ginger, garlic and onion whites in oil over medium-low, 1–2 minutes.
Stir in doubanjiang and miso for 15 seconds. Add sake, soy sauce and sesame.
Gradually stir in soy milk and prepared stock. Season; heat gently without boiling.
Blanch bok choy 2 minutes in boiling water. Remove; cook noodles following package timing and drain. Serve with broth, bok choy and onion greens.

recipes.title: Kitsune Udon with Kombu Broth
recipes.description: Udon soup with seasoned tofu pouches.
steps: Heat water and kombu over medium-low heat; remove kombu just before boiling.
Add mirin, sugar, soy sauce and salt. Bring to a simmer, then turn off heat.
Gently squeeze excess liquid from the seasoned tofu pouches. Slice green onion.
Boil udon following package directions, about 1 minute for frozen noodles. Drain thoroughly. Divide noodles and broth between bowls; add tofu and onion.

recipes.title: Vegan Poke Bowl
recipes.description: Vegetables and seasoned tofu over brown rice.
steps: Warm sesame oil over medium heat. Sauté onion, then tofu, coating it with oil.
Add soy sauce, vinegar and sambal. Reduce to medium-low; turn tofu through the sauce, then remove from heat.
Prepare the sliced vegetables. Squeeze lime over avocado; heat prepared rice if desired.
Arrange rice, vegetables, tofu and cooked edamame in bowls. Spoon over pan sauce; finish with sesame seeds and onions.

recipes.title: Soy-Glazed Eggplant Donburi
recipes.description: Glazed eggplant over prepared rice.
steps: Cut eggplant lengthwise into ¼-inch slices. Sprinkle with salt; rest 15 minutes, pat dry and coat with cornstarch.
Heat half the oil over medium heat. Cook eggplant in a single layer for 3–4 minutes. Add remaining oil, flip and cook 3–4 minutes.
Reduce to medium-low. Add mirin, soy sauce and ginger; simmer, spooning glaze over eggplant. Add a splash of water if overly thick.
Heat prepared rice as needed. Serve eggplant over rice, topped with sesame seeds and green onion.

recipes.title: Creamy Miso Pasta with Tofu and Asparagus
recipes.description: Soy-milk miso sauce with spaghetti.
steps: Whisk soy milk, miso and soy sauce until smooth.
Cook spaghetti in salted water for 1 minute less than package timing. Reserve the listed pasta water, then drain.
Warm tofu in olive oil over medium heat. Add asparagus, sauce salt and pepper.
Add the miso mixture and reserved pasta water. Warm over medium-low without boiling, until asparagus is tender.
Add spaghetti and toss over medium heat to finish cooking and coat with sauce.

recipes.title: Kabocha Macaroni Gratin
recipes.description: Individual squash gratins.
steps: Cook flour in four-fifths butter over low heat, 1–2 minutes. Whisk in milk and spices; stir 10–15 minutes until thick.
Sauté garlic and onion in oil. Cook mushrooms 2–3 minutes; add miso, squash and water. Cover; simmer until tender, 10 minutes.
Boil macaroni in salted water, 1 minute short of package timing. Drain; combine with vegetables and sauce. Season.
Grease dishes with remaining butter; add mixture, cheese and panko.
Broil 6 inches below heat for 3–4 minutes until golden. Rest 5 minutes.
